intended_use: Synthetic analytical software regression only; no physical validation.

assumptions.model: Rigid walls, incompressible irrotational flow, linear small displacement; viscosity, damping, wall flexibility and nonlinear response excluded.
assumptions.reference_points: Synthetic period ratios 1.1 and 8; frequencies only, no response histories.

derivation: Eigenmode basis: NASA SP-106, The Dynamic Behavior of Liquids in Moving Containers, with Applications to Space Vehicle Technology (1966 edition), section 2.2 'Rectangular Tank', equation (2.13b); https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/19670006555.
Incompressible irrotational flow gives Laplace(phi)=0 in a rigid rectangular tank.
For x in [0,L], z in [-h,0], impermeable boundaries admit phi_n proportional to cos(k_n*x)*cosh(k_n*(z+h)), k_n=n*pi/L.
Linear kinematic and dynamic free-surface conditions give omega_n^2=g*k_n*tanh(k_n*h), for positive integer n.
Odd and even modes are eigenmodes; their forcing coupling is not calculated.

Harmonic kinematics basis: OpenStax, University Physics Volume 1 (2016 edition), section 15.1 'Simple Harmonic Motion'; https://openstax.org/books/university-physics-volume-1/pages/15-1-simple-harmonic-motion.

Hydrostatic slope is derived from pressure-force balance: OpenStax, University Physics Volume 1 (2016 edition), sections 5.3 'Newton's Second Law' and 14.1 'Fluids, Density, and Pressure'; https://openstax.org/books/university-physics-volume-1/pages/5-3-newtons-second-law; https://openstax.org/books/university-physics-volume-1/pages/14-1-fluids-density-and-pressure.
Resolving pressure forces gives d(eta)/dx=-acceleration/g and the spatial end-to-end magnitude L*displacement*omega^2/g; this is not temporal peak-to-peak elevation.
